findings.title: Imported HTML and URL are stored and rendered without sanitization
findings.body: `contents` is appended directly to a footer that interpolates `url` into an HTML attribute, then the post is created with `cook_method: raw_html`. `Post#cook` returns raw HTML unchanged and the embed view renders `post.cooked` with `raw`. `PollFeed` supplies HTML-decoded feed content, so a feed item containing `<script>` or event attributes becomes stored XSS on the Discourse origin. Even if feed content were sanitized, a valid URL containing an apostrophe (for example a query value ending `...'onmouseover='...`) breaks out of this single-quoted href and injects an attribute. Sanitize imported content and safe URL schemes/attributes, and construct the attribution link with escaped URL helpers rather than string interpolation.

findings.title: The best embed template cannot be compiled
findings.body: `<%- end if %>` emits the Ruby tokens `end if` with no condition, which is invalid Ruby syntax. The template is compiled when an existing embedded topic is rendered, so after retrieval succeeds requests to `embed/best` will fail with a template syntax error instead of displaying the discussion. This must be a plain `end`.

findings.title: Remote import follows redirects outside the validated host
findings.body: The host check in `TopicRetriever` validates only the originally supplied URL, but `open(url).read` follows HTTP redirects and no subsequent destination is checked. A requester can select a path on the configured embeddable host; if that host has an open redirect, the Discourse server can be induced to fetch an arbitrary internal URL such as a cloud metadata endpoint. The Referer check does not prevent direct clients from sending a forged Referer header. Disable redirects or validate every redirect target's scheme, host, port, and resolved IP range before fetching.

findings.title: Embed creation is not atomic despite the unique URL index
findings.body: The code reads the embed row and only later creates it, with no lock or unique-conflict recovery. Concurrent feed polls/retrieval jobs can both observe no row and both create a topic; the loser then raises on the unique `embed_url` index. The outer transaction rolls back that loser, but `PostCreator` has already published MessageBus events and enqueued post-processing work before this transaction commits, leaving failed jobs/phantom notifications. Use an atomic create-or-find strategy (or rescue the unique violation and reload), and avoid publishing work until the outer transaction has committed.

findings.title: Each new embed request can trigger a complete feed import
findings.body: For every missing embed URL, retrieval synchronously invokes `PollFeed`, which downloads and parses the entire configured feed and iterates every item before attempting the requested page. The Redis throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so requests with distinct query strings bypass one another, and the public endpoint can queue those jobs with a forged Referer header. With feed polling enabled this permits unbounded feed downloads and import passes, exhausting workers and potentially overloading the feed source. Use a global feed-poll lock/cache (the existing `feed_key` is unused) and leave full polling to the scheduled job.

findings.title: Feed polling uses a String method unavailable on supported Ruby versions
findings.body: `String#scrub` was introduced in Ruby 2.1. This application still supports the Rails 3/4-era Ruby versions through its dual-boot Gemfile, including Ruby 1.9/2.0, where this line raises `NoMethodError` for every feed item and makes feed polling unusable. Use an encoding cleanup compatible with the supported Ruby versions or explicitly raise the minimum Ruby version.

findings.title: Adding the populated posts column in one step can lock and rewrite the table
findings.body: On the PostgreSQL versions contemporary with this application, adding a column with both a non-null default and `null: false` rewrites the entire `posts` table while holding a strong table lock. On a production forum this can block reads/writes for the duration of a large table rewrite during deployment. Add the column without a default/not-null constraint, backfill in batches, then set the default and constraint in later migrations.

findings.title: Non-root-relative links and images resolve against the Discourse embed URL
findings.body: `absolutize_urls` only rewrites values beginning with `/`. Common source markup such as `href="article.html"`, `href="../article"`, or `src="images/photo.jpg"` remains relative; when rendered inside the Discourse iframe, browsers resolve those URLs relative to `/embed/best` on the Discourse host rather than the imported article. This breaks links and assets for many imported pages. Resolve all relative href/src values against the source URL (for example with `URI.join`) while leaving already absolute URLs unchanged.
